text:
A kind woman who longed for a child was given a magical barleycorn by a fairy. She planted it, and it bloomed into a tulip. When the petals opened — inside sat a tiny, perfect little girl no bigger than a thumb!

The woman named her Thumbelina and loved her dearly.

One night, a large bumpy toad crept in and took sleeping Thumbelina away — she wanted her as a bride for her son! Thumbelina woke on a lily pad in the middle of a stream, crying and terrified.

Kind fish took pity and nibbled through the lily pad's stem to set her free.

Thumbelina drifted down the stream and spent the summer living in the meadow — sleeping in a flower, eating honey, and singing to the birds. She befriended a pretty butterfly who helped her float from flower to flower.

She was small, but she was free and happy.

But winter came and Thumbelina shivered in the cold. A kind field mouse took her in and offered warm shelter through winter. But the mouse's neighbor — a wealthy old mole — wanted to marry Thumbelina, even though she found the underground dark and gloomy.

Deep in the mole's tunnel, Thumbelina found a swallow who seemed to be dead. She secretly cared for him all winter, keeping him warm with leaves and singing to him.

And slowly — miraculously — the swallow recovered! He was alive!

When spring came, the grateful swallow offered to carry Thumbelina away to avoid her unhappy marriage to the mole. She climbed onto his back and they soared up into the blue sky together, away from the cold dark tunnel.

The swallow carried her to a land of warmth and flowers, where tiny flower fairies lived. Their handsome prince looked at Thumbelina with wonder. He had been searching for her kind forever. He placed a crown of flowers on her head and asked her to be his queen.

At last, Thumbelina was exactly where she belonged — surrounded by love and her own kind.

🌟 THE END 🌟

💡 Moral: You will always find where you truly belong!
